glossary_feedback.observation: No system-actor term for either end of a referral (D-11): this CapabilityStatement describes 'systems acting as referral sources' and invents names for the target's system ('delivery' system, 'a fulfilling system', 'referral recipient systems', 'referral sources system'). Left as-is per the domain notes; one glossary note would cover all of them.

The glossary treats referral source and referral target as fixed roles, but this CapabilityStatement expects referral sources also to receive referrals ('may sometimes also be recipients of requests for service', 'For referral sources that receive referrals from upstream systems', repeated across resources). Supports D-12's note that roles are assigned per referral.

The server section plans for a "'light' referral recipient that doesn't have local persistence or FHIR server capabilities", but the Direct and Indirect referral definitions require every party to have a FHIR server API (D-12).

In search-parameter documentation, 'individual' names any person a FHIR reference can point to (author, requester), not the subject of care. A strict D-2 option A would misapply 'patient' here; the R-PAT-INDIV pattern could skip 'organization or individual' and 'by a particular individual'.
